title: An experimental drilling apparatus used for evaluating drilling risks related to natural gas hydrate
author: Huang, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Prepare artificial core material
steps.instruction: Select and prepare the appropriate artificial core type (unconsolidated or consolidated) using quartz sand of 40–70 mesh (0.425 mm–0.212 mm).

substeps.instruction: For unconsolidated core: use quartz sand without additives, weigh approximately 8.2 kg, and keep it ready for packing.
For consolidated core: mix quartz sand with epoxy resin at a mass ratio of 1 part epoxy to 10 parts sand, combine to a total packed mass of about 10.0 kg.

steps.title: Pack core into high‑pressure vessel
steps.instruction: Tightly pack the prepared artificial core (either unconsolidated or consolidated) into the high‑pressure vessel ensuring no gaps.

steps.title: Set experimental temperature
steps.instruction: Adjust the cold room temperature to the desired experimental temperature before initiating pressure loading.

steps.title: Inject fluid and pressurize vessel
steps.instruction: Using a booster pump, inject the chosen gas or saline solution into the high‑pressure vessel until the vessel pressure reaches the desired value.

steps.title: Form hydrates in the core
steps.instruction: Maintain the set temperature and pressure to allow hydrates to form gradually within the packed artificial core.

steps.title: Prepare 40 wt% TBAB solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve tetrabutylammonium bromide (TBAB) in water to obtain a 40 wt% solution, which will produce type A TBAB hydrate (hydration number 26.0, congruent melting point 12 °C).

substeps.instruction: Inject the 40 wt% TBAB solution into the core (or replace the gas/saline) and allow type A TBAB hydrate to form under the set temperature and pressure.
